---
title: Data input
guide-section: "Results"
---

Whittaker uses [Narwhals](https://narwhals-dev.github.io/narwhals/) to accept any DataFrame library
without coupling the package to a specific backend.

## Supported backends

Any DataFrame that Narwhals supports works directly with `model.fit()` and `model.predict()`:

| Library | Install |
|---|---|
| [Polars](https://pola.rs/) | `pip install "whittaker[pl]"` |
| [Pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org/) | `pip install "whittaker[pd]"` |
| [PyArrow](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/) | `pip install "whittaker[pa]"` |
| [Modin](https://modin.readthedocs.io/) | no extra needed (Narwhals detects it) |
| [cuDF](https://docs.rapids.ai/api/cudf/stable/) | no extra needed |

## Usage example

```python
import polars as pl
import pandas as pd
import whittaker as wk

# Works with Polars
data_pl = pl.read_csv("data.csv")
model.fit(data_pl)

# Works with Pandas (same call, same result)
data_pd = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
model.fit(data_pd)
```

## Output format

Predictions and other tabular outputs use the same DataFrame type as the input by default. Pass
`format=` to override:

```python
preds = model.predict(data_pd, format="polars")   # always get a Polars frame
preds = model.predict(data_pl, format="pandas")   # always get a Pandas frame
```

## Narwhals internals

Internally Whittaker converts your frame to a Narwhals frame with `nw.from_native()`, extracts the
required columns, and converts to NumPy arrays for computation. The conversion is zero-copy for
Polars and Arrow-backed frames.

```python
import narwhals as nw

df = nw.from_native(your_dataframe)       # accepts any supported backend
arr = df["x"].to_numpy()                  # zero-copy for Polars/Arrow
```

## Missing values

GAMs do not support missing values in model predictors. Whittaker raises a clear error at fit time:

```
WhittakerError: Cannot fit model: column 'x1' contains 3 null values.

Options:
  1. Drop rows with nulls:   data.drop_nulls(["x1"])
  2. Set na_action="exclude" to drop and reindex predictions automatically.
```
